Article Title: Former Australian Test cricketer forced to retire at 27 sues school for head injury in 2014; here's why
Article Text:
Will Pucovski of Australia A lies injured after been struck in the helmet off the bowling of Kartik Tyagi of India A during International Tour match at Drummoyne Oval on December 08, 2020 in Sydney, Australia.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former Australia Test batter Will Pucovski has taken legal action against Melbourne private school Brighton Grammar, alleging it failed in its duty of care after the first concussion he suffered in 2014.According to reports in multiple Australian media outlets, Pucovski's lawyers have filed a statement of claim saying the school mishandled the head injury he suffered during an Australian rules football training session.Pucovski retired from professional cricket in April last year at the age of 27 after suffering 13 documented concussions during his career.The legal case centres on the first serious concussion he suffered as a teenager while playing football for Brighton Grammar. Pucovski was knocked unconscious during training, missed months of school after the incident, but returned to training within minutes of the hit.That injury became the first of 13 concussions he suffered before retiring from cricket on medical advice. His last match was for Victoria in 2024.Pucovski played one Test for Australia against India at the Sydney Cricket Ground in 2021. Opening the batting, he scored 62 in the first innings against an attack that included Jasprit Bumrah.He injured his shoulder while fielding during that match and missed the series-deciding Test at the Gabba. However, it was the repeated head injuries that eventually ended his cricket career.Speaking at a Lord's Taverners event earlier this year, Pucovski described how the 2014 incident changed his life."I literally got walked to the sidelines and then my only memory was the coach coming up to me and being like, 'Do you want to keep training?'. I am like, 'Yeah'. So I just went and trained for the rest of the day. It is probably the biggest day of my life in a weird way, because I have never felt the same since that day. I went from someone who would do anything and everything, to basically sitting on the couch doing nothing for an extended period," he had said, as quoted by Wisden.He developed blurred vision the following day and was admitted to hospital a week later.The International Concussion Society has warned about the risks of missed concussions in young athletes."The real concern starts when concussions are missed or inadequately addressed. This is particularly important to remember for young athletes and adolescents whose brains haven’t fully matured, which makes them more susceptible to serious brain injuries."Pucovski suffered his final serious concussion in March 2024 after being hit on the head by a ball from Riley Meredith during a Sheffield Shield match. Following advice from an independent medical panel, he retired from professional cricket at the age of 27.
Article Summary: Former Australia Test batter Will Pucovski has taken legal action against Melbourne private school Brighton Grammar. He is alleging it failed in its duty of care after the first concussion he suffered in 2014. That injury became the first of 13 concussions he suffered before retiring from cricket on medical advice.

Article Title: 'A tricky one': Rahul Dravid reveals big concern over Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's Test future
Article Text:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (AFP Photo)

'I'm not sure about that'

Eight runs with the bat, two wickets with the ball

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's journey in white-ball cricket has moved at remarkable speed. At just 15, the left-handed batter has already represented India and made his presence felt at the international level.Sooryavanshi ended the IPL 2026 season as Rajasthan Royals ' highest run-scorer with 776 runs. He then produced another explosive performance, smashing 94 off 29 balls against Sri Lanka 'A' in the List A tri-series final in Colombo.He made his senior India debut against England in July and followed it up with an impressive tour of Zimbabwe. Sooryavanshi finished the series with 151 runs, the most by any batter, and was named Player of the Series.He has scored 193 runs in six T20I innings at a strike rate of 189.21.However, his progress in red-ball cricket has been slower. Sooryavanshi has played eight first-class matches and averages 17.25. He is now playing for East Zone in the Duleep Trophy as he looks to gain more experience in the longer format.Former India head coach Rahul Dravid , who worked with Sooryavanshi at Rajasthan Royals, believes the teenager has the talent to succeed in Test cricket.But he feels there is one major hurdle - finding enough time to play domestic red-ball cricket."With Vaibhav, you've got to be patient. He's only 15 years old, and from what I've seen of the kid, I have no doubt that, given the opportunity to practice and play domestic cricket and a couple of seasons of red-ball cricket, he will be able to hold his own in a Test match team. Whether he'll be able to break into the XI with the guys already performing, that's a different story and a tricky one," Dravid told JioHotstar.Dravid's concern is not about Sooryavanshi's ability. Instead, he is worried about whether the teenager will get enough opportunities because of his growing international commitments."Whether he'll have the time to play two full seasons of domestic cricket because he'll be so busy playing for India in the white-ball format, I'm not sure about that. So skill-wise, I think there is no problem; whether he will be able to do it because of schedules might be a bit more tricky."Sooryavanshi had a quiet outing with the bat in East Zone's Duleep Trophy quarter-final against North East Zone. The 15-year-old scored eight runs from six deliveries before Bishworjit Konthoujam dismissed him.He quickly made up for it with the ball.The East Zone vice-captain picked up two wickets in just four deliveries, showing that he could contribute even when things did not go his way with the bat.Sooryavanshi picked up his third first-class wicket with the second delivery of the 28th over. He bowled a three-quarter-length delivery outside off stump, prompting Kishan Lyngdoh to come down the track and attack. Lyngdoh tried to hit the ball hard but failed to keep his shape and produced a leading edge towards cover. Denish Das, who was fielding as a substitute, completed the catch.Three deliveries later, Sooryavanshi struck again. This time, he bowled a good-length delivery around off stump to Imliwati Lemtur. The batter tried to defend from the crease but only managed a thin outside edge. Ishan Kishan reacted quickly behind the stumps and completed the catch.
Article Summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi made his senior India debut against England in July. The 15-year-old has scored 193 runs in six T20I innings at a strike rate of 189.21. Former India head coach Rahul Dravid believes the teenager has the talent to succeed in Test cricket.

Article Title: India’s listless Hockey World Cup show sparks alarm
Article Text:
India's Dilpreet Singh in action during the World Cup Field Hockey pool D match between India and Pakistan in Amstelveen, Netherlands.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: If the eighth place in the FIH Pro League sounded the warning bells, the Indian men’s hockey team has done little to show they heard it.On Friday, India will play Belgium in the 7-8 classification match of the World Cup. Monday’s 3-5 defeat to Argentina summed up a campaign littered with familiar flaws. There have been moments of promise in Amstelveen, but they have been overshadowed by defensive lapses, poor decision-making and an attack that has often failed to convert pressure into goals. Craig Fulton has fought to keep the players Hockey India was looking beyond; the South African got what he wanted to prepare the team, but does not have much to show in terms of results.In five matches, India conceded 16 goals, while scoring 14, five of which were field goals. Off the 25 penalty corners earned, they converted seven, six of them by skipper Harmanpreet Singh Former India player and coach Jagbir Singh was scathing in his assessment of the team’s performance. He questioned the way India has approached the post-Olympic transition. “We have to stick to the Olympic cycle and prepare teams. After the Olympics is the period when you need to look ahead and prepare a team that can go from one Olympic year to the next and then maybe extend it based on their performance.Which was not the case in this team. I don’t agree with a few selections, but it's all about the coach’s choice,” the 61-year-old explained. A “lack of consistency” was India’s biggest failing, said Jagbir.For most of their campaign, the Indian defence crumbled under pressure. “Experienced players like Hardik were short of ideas, and the defenders looked clueless. Against Argentina are the trickiest team, we didn’t have players to take care of their players who were making all the difference,” pointed out the former India player. He was particularly critical of India’s midfield. “Which team can survive without a strong midfield in hockey? Where was India’s midfield?”“We have a good midfield, but we didn’t even know what the transition of play was or how to attack from defence. Either we couldn't understand the coach's plan, or we couldn't adapt our strategy to the opponents,” he stated. The Indian team will have less than three weeks to pull their act together and head to Japan for the Asian Games, with an LA Olympics berth at stake for the defending champions.
Article Summary: India's World Cup campaign has been littered with familiar flaws. India conceded 16 goals, while scoring 14, five of which were field goals. Former India player and coach Jagbir Singh was scathing in his assessment of the team’s performance.

Article Title: 'I was not a good national team coach': Manolo Marquez
Article Text:
Manolo Marquez

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: Manolo Marquez has admitted he was “not a good national team coach” during his brief stint with India, accepting responsibility for a disappointing run while arguing that structural issues in Indian football made the job even more difficult.In his 11 months in charge of the Indian national team, a post he left a year ago, India won one of eight matches, and it was a friendly against the low-ranked Maldives.Marquez, who is beginning his seventh season in India and his third ISL club assignment with Mumbai City FC , was blunt when asked what he learnt from his time as India coach.“I think that the results were bad. I was not a good national team coach,” he said. “When you play eight games, and you win only one, it’s not good. I called 51 players in eight games, which is too much. I never found the correct group.”The Spaniard, however, believes his record cannot be viewed in isolation. He pointed to the disparity between India and several of their Asian opponents, particularly the increasing presence of overseas-born or foreign-origin players in rival national teams.“When you don’t play with the same conditions, the opponent is very difficult,” he said.Marquez also recalled the impact of players such as Ryan Williams, who scored for India shortly after being introduced, and Hamza Choudhury, whose presence transformed Bangladesh.But the former FC Goa coach was clear that he would not use those factors to escape responsibility.“I am the first person guilty, and I don’t want to avoid responsibility,” he said. “There are a lot of factors, but one factor was that I was not the correct person in that moment.”Marquez also revealed that despite widespread reports, he had no difficulty combining his India role with his responsibilities at FC Goa, saying he had been caught between criticism that he was prioritising the club and criticism that he was not doing enough for the national team.His wider diagnosis of Indian football was equally stark. The 58-year-old believes the biggest issue lies in how players are prepared before they reach the professional level.“For me, the problem is in how they arrive. Most of them arrive without the correct knowledge in professional football,” he said.Marquez feels the gap in professionalism between Indian players and those from established football nations remains significant, pointing to nutrition, training, recovery, sleep and strength conditioning as areas that need improvement.“Obviously, the attitude to get better is there. But still, I think that we need to improve in some very important aspects. I think that most of the Indian players go to the gym, but I'm not sure that most of the players know what the correct thing to do at the gym is. So you get my point,” he said.He also believes foreigners remain decisive in the ISL. Last season, teams operated with differing numbers of overseas players, with East Bengal and Mohun Bagan winning the top two positions while Mumbai, despite using fewer foreigners, emerged as the strongest side operating with four.“The foreigners are the difference in Indian football,” Marquez said. “But obviously, the level of the Indian players is very important. With good Indian players, you will have more possibilities to win the ISL than without them.”
Article Summary: Manolo Marquez admits he was "not a good national team coach" during his brief stint with India. Former FC Goa coach accepts responsibility for disappointing run. Spaniard argues structural issues in Indian football made the job even more difficult. India won one of eight matches under Marquez.

Article Title: Durand Cup triumph a whiff of redemption for Edmund and Habas
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOLKATA: When people’s paths cross, sometimes it comes with the whiff of a road movie evolving and eventually moving their journey towards its point of redemption with a profound sense of inevitability.For Edmund Lalrindika and Antonio Lopez Habas — the two main characters of East Bengal FC’s audacious dismantling of Mohun Bagan SG on their way to winning the Durand Cup here on Sunday, their journeys perhaps wield a symbolism with much depth and emotional nuance. They are about returning to the battle front not only to survive a seemingly insurmountable ordeal but completing an unfinished business with a beguiling element of defiance.Six years ago it was at the very Salt Lake Stadium, Edmund saw his journey suffer an unexpected setback. Five days after joining an Alejandro Menendez’s East Bengal on a short-term loan deal from Bengaluru FC, the Mizo youngster made debut in the first-leg I-League derby in the 2019-2020 season, coming off the bench to provide an assist for Macros Jimenez’s goal in a match which Mohun Bagan eventually won 2-1. It was the penultimate I-League derby between the two traditional rivals before their foray into the Indian Super League which was coronated as the country’s top-tier league. Edmund’s stay in the match was merely 14-minute long as it was cut short with a serious injury, forcing him to leave the field and return to the BFC fold.Two years later, another spine injury put a serious question mark over his future, with his doctors having advised to stay away from football. But Edmund defied the odds with his customary grit and a year after joining Inter Kashi, he found in Habas a catalyst he had been waiting to process his rebirth with a structure of meaning.If Edmund’s journey to self-realization was marinated in suffering, the one for Habas had a smidge of rejection. Having returned to take charge of Mohun Bagan Super Giant midway in the 2023-2024 season and guided them to the ISL Winners’ Shield, the veteran Spanish coach didn’t find any backers from the team management to continue and took the plunge into the second tier of Indian club football with Inter Kashi.Edmund — already becoming the first player from I-League to earn a call-up in the senior national team since ISL’s promotion to the top league — welcomed the Spaniard to the newly-formed team with a late winner, helping Inter Kashi edge past SC Bengaluru at Kalyani stadium on Nov 24 in 2024. Habas went on to transform his precious pupil from a winger to an attacker, often employing him as a False 9 position. The result was dazzling for the duo and devastating for the rivals. As Inter Kashi eventually won the I-League and earned their promotion to ISL, Edmund made his choice — returning to East Bengal and completing a mission he had left unfinished.When Habas left his position as Inter Kashi coach three matches before the end of the 2025-2026 season and returned to Spain amid uncertainty over ISL’s future, East Bengal too were forced to search for a new beginning, days after winning the ISL. Coach Oscar Bruzon had already made his intention of leaving clear to everyone and investor Emami Group was unwilling to pump in money in the red-and-gold project.The club officials had to step in and when Habas received a call from them to take reins of the new ISL champions, he was always game for a homecoming with a difference.As fate would have it, Edmund reunited with his mentor and the duo created quite a buzz on Sunday.“I’ve not won the Durand Cup in my career. So, it’s a special one,” Habas told reporters after the final.“Hopefully, it’s just the start of a new journey and more trophies will follow,” a beaming Edmund remarked.
Article Summary: Edmund Lalrindika and Antonio Lopez Habas are the two main characters of East Bengal FC’s audacious dismantling of Mohun Bagan SG on their way to winning the Durand Cup here on Sunday. Their journeys perhaps wield a symbolism with much depth and emotional nuance. They are about returning to the battle front not only to survive a seemingly insurmountable ordeal but completing an unfinished business.

Article Title: 'They've fallen behind a little bit': Rahul Dravid on Team India's WTC final hopes
Article Text:

New Zealand challenge awaits

Australia series another big test

NEW DELHI: Former India head coach Rahul Dravid believes India still have a chance of reaching the World Test Championship final, but their path has become tougher. India have slipped behind in the race and will need strong results in their remaining matches to make the top two.India are currently fifth in the WTC points table and face a difficult away series against New Zealand before hosting Australia in a five-Test series from January 2027.India have made a strong start to their ongoing series in Sri Lanka, leading 1-0 after winning the first Test in Galle by 165 runs. They have also taken control of the second Test after a big batting effort.Dravid feels the Sri Lanka series is an important first step, but India still have plenty of work to do."I'm hoping they do. It'll be a great run if India can qualify for the WTC final from here," Dravid told 'JioStar' when asked if India would be able to make the summit clash from here."They've fallen behind a little bit, but the kind of quality that the Indian team has, you're not going to write them off at any stage. They started off well against Sri Lanka, so that's a good first step," he said.India will travel to New Zealand in October for two Tests.Dravid expects the series to be a major test, especially for the younger players who have limited experience of playing in those conditions."(Playing against) New Zealand away, (is) always a challenge. (They are a) tough team, New Zealand, to play away from home. A lot of the young Indian boys have not played in those conditions, so that's going to be a big challenge," he said.Dravid also pointed out that India will miss the experience of several senior players who are no longer part of the Test side."Hopefully, they can keep the guys fit and not have a lot of injuries over the next few months. We're missing the experience of Virat (Kohli) and Rohit (Sharma), Ajinkya Rahane and (Cheteshwar) Pujara, these kinds of guys who've probably been there the last time India went. So that will be an interesting series as well," Dravid added.After New Zealand, India will host Australia in a five-Test Border-Gavaskar Trophy series from January 2027. Dravid expects the Australian players to be highly motivated after failing to win a Test series in India in recent years."Australia will be really exciting. A lot of their players will be very keen to do well in India. That's a generation of truly great Australian players, a great Australian team that has not won in India. So they'll be keen to do that," Dravid said.
Article Summary: Former India head coach Rahul Dravid believes India still have a chance of reaching the World Test Championship final. India are currently fifth in the WTC points table and face a difficult away series against New Zealand before hosting Australia in a five-Test series from January 2027.

Article Title: Praggnanandhaa storms into Grand Chess Tour final with 19-9 win over Vincent Keymer
Article Text:
Indian Grandmaster R Praggnanandhaa (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Indian Grandmaster R Praggnanandhaa secured his place in the final of the last leg of the Grand Chess Tour with a commanding 19-9 victory over Germany’s Vincent Keymer.Praggnanandhaa will now face pre-event favourite and defending champion Fabiano Caruana of the USA in the title clash.The Indian entered the final day with a six-point advantage after winning the second Classical game against Keymer. With the competition moving to shorter formats, Praggnanandhaa wasted little time in strengthening his position.He won both Rapid games against Keymer to establish an unassailable 17-3 lead. Another victory in the opening Blitz game took Praggnanandhaa to 19 points and confirmed his place in the final.The remaining Blitz games still had to be completed under the tournament rules, and Keymer managed to finish strongly by winning the final three Blitz encounters. However, the German’s late surge could not alter the outcome as Praggnanandhaa had already secured a decisive advantage.Caruana also booked his place in the final after defeating fellow American Wesley So 18-9. The defending champion’s performance in the faster formats proved decisive, particularly during the Blitz games.Caruana had not traditionally been regarded as a dominant player in faster formats, but his performance on Monday showed that he could challenge that perception when it mattered.The Grand Chess Tour finale carries a total prize purse of USD 450,000, with USD 200,000 going to the winner and USD 125,000 to the losing finalist.Although Caruana enters the final as the favourite, Praggnanandhaa has already shown he can thrive under pressure and will look to produce another strong performance against the defending champion.In the third-place play-off, Keymer will meet another American, Wesley So. The top three finishers at the event will earn direct invitations to next year’s Grand Chess Tour.Semifinal results:R Praggnanandhaa (India, 19) beat Vincent Keymer (Germany, 9)Fabiano Caruana (USA, 18) beat Wesley So (USA, 9)
Article Summary: Indian Grandmaster R Praggnanandhaa secured his place in the final of the last leg of the Grand Chess Tour with a commanding 19-9 victory over Germany’s Vincent Keymer. He will now face pre-event favourite and defending champion Fabiano Caruana of the USA in the title clash.

Article Title: Zeeshan Ansari: 'India A and IPL exposure has made me a better leg-spinner'
Article Text:

Zeeshan Ansari plays for Merrut Mavericks in the UPT20 League (Photo Courtesy: UPT20 League)

I feel my career has been made because of the UPT20 League. I wasn't playing much cricket and my name wasn't known anywhere. Zeeshan Ansari

NEW DELHI: Zeeshan Ansari went six years in cricket's red-ball wilderness. After playing for Uttar Pradesh against Tamil Nadu in the Ranji Trophy in January 2020, the legspinner admitted that he found it difficult to bowl with the red cherry. The influx of T20 competitions had accustomed him to the white ball over the red.That time away ended when the 26-year-old earned a surprise call-up to the India A squad for the Sri Lanka tour. The comeback didn't get a dream Bollywood-esque start. He gave away 76 runs in 19 overs in the first innings in Galle. He was then hammered for 29 runs in the four overs he bowled in the second essay.The Lucknow-born leggie admitted that the comeback had been a 'little difficult'. He sees this as a learning curve, with the exposure making him a better bowler."It was a good learning experience. I played red-ball cricket after so many years, and I got to learn a lot. There were a lot of good batsmen I was bowling against. The Sri Lankan batters are good players of spin. And I was also bowling with the Kookaburra ball for the first time. It was a different experience for me," he says.Interestingly, Zeeshan had garnered attention early in his career because of his exploits with the red ball.At the U-19 Cooch Behar Trophy in 2014-15, the UP player took 40 wickets, which helped him get into the 2016 U-19 World Cup squad. He picked up 30 wickets in the CK Nayudu Trophy in 2016-17 and was rewarded immediately as he was selected for the Ranji Trophy the following year. He made an impressive debut under the captaincy of Suresh Raina. Zeeshan picked up six wickets in the match but was dropped for the next fixture. In the next four seasons, he played four more games until 2020, before he was left in the wilderness.Then, earlier this year, he got a surprise call-up first as a net bowler for the one-off Test against Afghanistan in Chandigarh, followed by his India A selection. A day before the Test match against Afghanistan, Ansari was seen having a long conversation with Team India head coach Gautam Gambhir."Gautam sir just told me that I am doing well and should keep bowling like this, just as I have been. There is nothing else to think about. Just keep performing. It was a good conversation, and it boosted my confidence," he recalls.The exposure, Zeeshan feels, has made him a better bowler, and he has learnt more about his bowling and what exactly he needs to do to find more success."I have now played in the IPL , gone with India A, met a lot of people and worked with some really good coaches. All of that has helped me understand my cricket better and learn what can work for me and what I need to do to be successful. For instance, I have realised that I need to bowl a little slower and put more revs on the ball. I have kept that in mind, and that is what I am working on," he says."I learnt that you should bowl as much as you can with the red ball. Whatever variations you have, you should work on them well and then try to execute them in matches. The most important thing is repetition. Repetition is very important for a leg-spinner. I have practised so much that I am now able to bring variations into my googlies as well," he adds.Zeeshan, who plays for Sunrisers Hyderabad (SRH) in the Indian Premier League (IPL), credits the UP T20 League for giving his career a new lease of life."I feel my career has been made because of the UPT20 League. I wasn't playing much cricket and my name wasn't known anywhere. In the first season of the league, I won the Purple Cap with 24 wickets to my name, and that's when people started recognising me," he says.Zeeshan is still 26 and now, with selectors tracking his development closely, he will hopefully get more chances for his state team. This time around, he won't have to live in the wilderness.
Article Summary: Zeeshan Ansari went six years in cricket's red-ball wilderness. The 26-year-old earned a surprise call-up to the India A squad for the Sri Lanka tour. The Lucknow-born leggie admitted that the comeback had been a 'little difficult'

Article Title: $7 million! AG.AL crowned Esports World Cup 2026 club champion after landmark Paris edition
Article Text:
AG.AL crowned Esports World Cup 2026 Club Champion (Pic credit: EWC 2026)

AG.AL complete remarkable campaign

Paris delivers record numbers

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

AG.AL were crowned Esports World Cup 2026 club champions after a dramatic final weekend in Paris, securing the $7 million (~INR 66.9 crore) top prize following seven weeks of record-breaking esports action featuring more than 2,000 players, 200 Clubs and 25 tournaments across 24 games.AG.AL finished on 5,300 points, edging two-time defending champions Team Falcons, who ended runners-up with 4,600 points. Team Vitality finished third with 3,300 points, followed by Natus Vincere (2,950) and Team Liquid (2,700).The club championship went down to the wire, with AG.AL completing their campaign through Gwendal “Gwen” Duparc's victory in the inaugural Trackmania tournament. The Frenchman delivered under pressure to win the tournament and secure the club championship for AG.AL.Falcons had entered the Trackmania playoffs at the top of the overall standings, but Carl-Antoni “Carl Jr.” Cloutier's quarterfinal exit opened the door for AG.AL. Gwen then dominated the final, securing the $130,000 (~INR 1.2 crore) tournament prize and, more importantly, the club championship.AG.AL's title-winning campaign also featured a first-place finish in Tekken 8, second-place finishes in Chess, Free Fire and the Honor of Kings World Cup, and a third-place finish in Teamfight Tactics.“When we began expanding AG.AL globally in 2024, the same year the Esports World Cup launched, we set out to build a Club capable of succeeding across games, regions and cultures. This title shows how far that vision has come,” said Eddy Chen, COO at AG.AL.“Our journey in Paris reflected the strength of the entire organization, from M. Zubair’s breakthrough in TEKKEN 8 and our deep runs across multiple titles to Gwen delivering the decisive Trackmania victory under extraordinary pressure. But this trophy belongs equally to every player, coach and staff member whose dedication brought us here.”The Paris edition also produced several memorable individual performances. France's Caliste “Caliste” Henry-Hennebert led Karmine Corp to the League of Legends Grand Final in front of a home crowd, while 15-year-old Chilean Jaime “Craime” Bustos became the youngest Esports World Cup champion after defeating two EVO champions.AG.AL's Khawaja “M. Zubair” also captured the Tekken 8 title, while Rocket League star Samy “dralii” Hajji became the first three-time Esports World Cup champion. Grandmaster Magnus Carlsen successfully defended his Chess title without losing a game.The 2026 edition set new benchmarks for the Esports World Cup, with the event reaching 850 million viewers and generating 440 million hours watched — increases of 13% and 26%, respectively, year-on-year. Peak viewership reached 4.3 million during the League of Legends tournament.The event was distributed globally through more than 100 broadcast and OTT partners in 47 languages, with 5,000 creators and co-streamers supporting its coverage.In another major milestone, 175,000 tickets were sold for esports competitions, a 94% increase from 2025. Total visits across competition venues, Fan Fest and city activations exceeded two million during the seven-week event.“We are proud of what the Esports World Cup has achieved in Paris and of its continued international growth,” said His Royal Highness Prince Faisal bin Bandar bin Sultan al Saud, Chairman of the Executive Committee of the Esports Foundation.“Bringing the EWC to a global audience beyond Saudi Arabia marks an important milestone in its journey and reflects the growing recognition of esports as a global industry, connecting communities, cultures and audiences around the world.”Paris was the first city outside Riyadh to host the Esports World Cup. More than 22,600 campaign placements across the capital reached 94% of Parisians, while the final weekend's Counter-Strike tournament was staged at the 20,000-seat Accor Arena.The event followed a year-long competitive journey involving more than 1.5 million players across 330 Road to EWC events.“Our ambition has always been bigger than a single event: to grow esports and establish it as a leading global sport,” said Ralf Reichert, Chief Executive Officer of the Esports Foundation.The Esports World Cup will return to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, in 2027.
Article Summary: AG.AL win $7 million (~INR 66.9 crore) top prize following seven weeks of record-breaking esports action. AG.AL finished on 5,300 points, edging two-time defending champions Team Falcons, who ended runners-up with 4,600 points. More than 2,000 players, 200 Clubs and 25 tournaments across 24 games.

Article Title: Rohan Bopanna hits out at Asian Games tennis-squad cuts
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: “Let sport decide, not a spreadsheet.” That was the sharp message from twotime Asian Games gold medallist Rohan Bopannaas the pruning of India’s tennis squad by the sports ministry for the Aichi-Nagoya Games triggered a fresh debate over selection policy.Bopanna backed five players who have been dropped from the 12-member list recommended by the All India Tennis Association (AITA), questioning the wisdom of deciding medal prospects before players have stepped on to the court.“If outcomes are already decided, why have qualifications at all? Article Title: ‘Save women’s HIL’: Indian hockey stars make emotional plea as league faces uncertain future
Article Text:
Indian women's hockey team (Pic credit: Hockey India)

‘HIL has benefited us a lot’

Salima Tete highlights talent pathway

‘HIL has given me confidence’

Navneet urges corporate sector to step in

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What aspect of the HIL do you think benefits players the most? Exposure to high-level competition. Confidence building. Talent identification. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Financial challenges threaten women's HIL

NEW DELHI: India’s women hockey players have made an emotional appeal to save the Women’s Hockey India League (HIL), insisting that the competition has played a crucial role in building the confidence of a young side that is on the brink of its best-ever World Cup finish since 1974.With 11 World Cup debutants in the squad, India have suffered only one defeat against Olympic champions the Netherlands and held Olympic silver medallists China to a 2-2 draw in their opening match. A goalless draw against Australia ended their hopes of reaching the semifinals, but India will now play for fifth and sixth place — a finish that would still be their best at the World Cup in 52 years.The players believe the Women's HIL has been central to their progress and fear its discontinuation could damage the pathway for the next generation.Veteran midfielder Neha, who led Odisha Warriors to the inaugural HIL title in the 2024-25 season, stressed the importance of the league in giving young players access to a higher level of competition.“I think we have done our best to inspire girls in India to hold a hockey stick. People prefer their kids to play individual sports, but this should give them hope,” Neha told PTI.“In the last two years, HIL for women has benefited us a lot. Junior and senior Nationals do not have this level of competition.Women's HIL has given us players like Baljeet, Sakshi and Rutuja, who are part of this World Cup team. For upcoming players also, we need this league. It should not be discontinued.”Captain Salima Tete also underlined how the league has helped widen India's talent pool and given emerging players a route into the national setup.“We have many players from HIL in the Indian team. They get a chance to be selected for the national camp, which is an important opportunity for them,” she said.“This is just the beginning for us and there is much more to achieve. For that, HIL is a must so that our talent pool is broadened and the girls get good exposure to handling the pressure of international hockey.”Sakshi Rana, another player who has benefited from the league, said the experience of playing alongside established international stars helped her handle pressure on the biggest stage.“HIL has given me confidence, which was very useful in this tournament. It is about handling pressure. We have played alongside many veteran players like World Cup top scorer Yibbi Janssen and learnt a lot,” she said.Navneet Kaur said the league also helped younger players overcome the fear of facing established international stars.“We have been playing HIL for the last two years and gained confidence from that. We have played with some of the biggest names in international hockey and after sharing the dressing room with them, the fear and hesitation was gone,” she said.“That gave us self-belief. We often discuss that they are like us and we can beat them because we have played with them.”Navneet also urged franchises and corporate houses to step in as the women's league faces financial uncertainty.“We have heard that a few teams are pulling out of the Women's HIL, but at a time when our performance graph is going up, we want to request them to support us. It will be a big setback for women's hockey and the future crop of players,” she said.“I request the Sports Ministry and Hockey India to save this league. I also request the corporate sector, which invests huge money in cricket, to support women's hockey.“Our league does not require that much money. It is not about money, we need exposure. Women's Hockey League should survive. We will do even better in the future,” added Navneet, who was player of the tournament last season with the Delhi team.The appeal comes as the revived women's HIL grapples with high operating costs, low broadcast and ticket revenues, delayed player payments and limited sponsorship interest. Franchise sources said the league is currently not commercially viable, with the cost of running both a men's and women's HIL team estimated at around Rs 10-12 crore, including an administrative fee of around Rs 1 crore. The women's franchise fee of Rs 2.5 crore, however, has been removed for the third season.
Article Summary: Women's Hockey India League (HIL) facing financial uncertainty. Players say league has helped build confidence of young side. India on brink of best-ever World Cup finish since 1974. Captain Salima Tete: HIL has given emerging players route into national setup.

Article Title: BCCI AGM in Mumbai on September 18 to discuss associate membership for Andaman & Nicobar Islands

MUMBAI: The Board of Control for Cricket in India ( BCCI ) will hold its Annual General Meeting at its headquarters here on September 18, as per a notification sent by BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia to the member associations.One of the key items on the agenda is the nomination of India’s representative to the International Cricket Council (ICC).Interestingly, one of the items on the agenda is the “grant of associate membership to Cricket Association of Andaman & Nicobar Island of the Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands.”The proposal had come up for discussion at an earlier Apex Council meeting of the BCCI and will now be placed before the AGM for consideration. If approved, the move would bring the Union Territory into the BCCI fold. Associate membership, however, does not carry voting rights. The BCCI will also induct one representative of the Indian Cricketers’ Association into the IPL Governing Council.The meeting is expected to ratify the appointment of the new five-member junior selection committee, for which the BCCI had recently taken out an advertisement.
Article Summary: The Board of Control for Cricket in India will hold its Annual General Meeting on September 18. One of the key items on the agenda is the nomination of India’s representative to the International Cricket Council. Article Title: Late-order roadblock: Sonal Dinusha's 85, support from tail leave Sri Lanka 38 runs away from follow-on; India remain in control
Article Text:
Sri Lanka's Sonal Dinusha on day three of the second Test cricket match between India and Sri Lanka, in Colombo, Sri Lanka. (PTI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

If it’s Devdutt Padikkal and Dhruv Jurel that have emerged as India’s batting stars of the future in this series, Sonal Dinusha is making a similar statement for Sri Lanka. The left-hander followed his scores of 100 and 84 in Galle with an unbeaten 85 (137b, 2x6) to lead a gritty fightback on a rain-hit third day of the second Test at SSC on Tuesday.Dinusha found an able ally in fellow youngster Pasindu Sooriyabandara, who struck 80 (133b, 9x4) in only his second Test innings, as Sri Lanka frustrated India for large parts of the day before ending on 265 for eight. The hosts still require 38 runs to avoid the follow-on after India posted 503 for nine declared, but the resistance shown by their young batting brigade has ensured they remain in the contest.Dinusha, now the leading run-scorer of the series with 269 runs at 134.50, was closing in on a second Test century in as many matches when rain and bad light forced an early finish to the proceedings. Together with Lahiru Kumara (8 batting), he added an unbeaten 35-run stand for the ninth wicket, after earlier sharing a crucial 57-run partnership with Keshara Nuwantha (18).The 25-year-old has now registered three consecutive 80-plus scores in the series, underlining his credentials as a long-term solution to Sri Lanka’s batting woes in the middle order. With Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Mendis and Dinesh Chandimal unavailable, Dinusha has shouldered responsibility admirably.India had appeared well placed to secure a sizeable lead and potentially enforce the follow-on after reducing Sri Lanka to 216/7. However, Dinusha and the lower order displayed plenty of resolve to blunt the visitors’ bowling attack.Earlier, Sri Lanka showed intent from the outset. Sooriyabandara and Kamindu Mendis (32) stitched together an 87-run third-wicket partnership, helping the hosts add 122 runs while losing only two wickets in the opening session.Sooriyabandara brought up his maiden Test fifty off 76 balls before falling to Ravindra Jadeja while attempting a late cut.Prasidh Krishna was India’s standout bowler, returning figures of 3/57. The pacer provided the early breakthrough when debutant opener Kamil Mishara (19) gloved a sharply rising delivery to wicketkeeper Dhruv Jurel. Prasidh later removed Kamindu with another short ball.Manav Suthar then dismissed captain Dhananjaya de Silva for 8 with a delivery that spun away sharply, while Mohammed Siraj accounted for Niroshan Dickwella, who gloved a leg-side catch to wicketkeeper Jurel for a duck.Yet, Sri Lanka refused to surrender. Aided by interruptions and determined lower-order resistance, Dinusha ensured India were left waiting for the final two wickets.
Article Summary: Sonal Dinusha scores unbeaten 85 to lead Sri Lanka fightback on third day of second Test. Sri Lanka end on 265 for eight after India posted 503 for nine declared. Dinusha is now the leading run-scorer of the series with 269 runs at 134.50.

Article Title: ‘Incredibly emotional’: Anaya Bangar gets Cricket Australia nod for elite women’s cricket, eyes WBBL
Article Text:
Anaya Bangar (Pic credit: Bangar's Instagram post)

Eligibility secured, but WBBL place must still be earned

From uncertainty to a pathway in Australia

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Anaya Bangar has taken a major step towards returning to competitive cricket after Cricket Australia confirmed that she will be eligible to play elite women’s cricket in the country from March 2027.Bangar, who underwent gender-affirming surgery in March, received the confirmation under Cricket Australia’s Inclusion of Transgender and Gender Diverse Players in Elite Cricket Policy. The decision opens a pathway for her to pursue a place in the Women’s Big Bash League (WBBL), although she stressed that eligibility does not guarantee a franchise contract.In an exclusive conversation with Bombay Times, Anaya, daughter of former India all-rounder and batting coach Sanjay Bangar , described the development as an emotional moment after fearing that her cricket career had ended following her transition.“I am now eligible to play in the Women’s Big Bash League (WBBL) in Australia from March 2027 onwards. For me, this is incredibly emotional because there was a point when I genuinely believed I had lost cricket forever,” she told Bombay Times.“Cricket has been such a fundamental part of my identity since childhood, and having to step away from the sport after my transition was one of the hardest things I experienced. So this isn’t simply about being included in a women’s league.It represents the possibility of returning to the sport I deeply love,” she said.Anaya was quick to clarify that Cricket Australia’s decision only provides her with the opportunity to pursue elite women’s cricket. She will still have to earn a place in a WBBL squad through her performances.“Cricket Australia has allowed me to pursue elite women’s cricket in Australia. The next challenge is to get myself into the best possible physical and competitive shape and put myself in a position to be considered by a WBBL franchise. I still have to train, compete, perform and earn that opportunity,” she said.She explained that the WBBL’s overseas-player contracting and draft system means she will have to convince a franchise of her value.“The WBBL has an overseas-player contracting and draft system, where clubs select from the pool of available international players, like it happens in the IPL or the WPL,” Anaya said.“So ultimately, I still have to convince a franchise that I can contribute to their team. For me, that means getting back into competitive cricket in Australian leagues, working on my batting, bowling, fielding and fitness, training consistently and demonstrating that I can perform at that level.”The development comes against the backdrop of different policies governing transgender participation in cricket.Cricket Australia has a different framework for elite domestic cricket, allowing transgender women who meet its eligibility and testosterone-related criteria to participate.Anaya said she had hoped for a clearer pathway in India but eventually chose to focus on what she could control.“When you grow up playing cricket competitively, the idea of potentially never being able to play again is incredibly difficult,” she said.“But I’ve also learned that I can’t build my future around waiting for somebody else to make a decision. I had to focus on what I could control — my health, my transition, my performance, the scientific evidence, and having conversations with sporting organisations.”She added: “I’m grateful that I have a pathway in Australia, and I hope that my journey can contribute to a broader conversation about how sporting bodies can approach transgender participation with both fairness and inclusion.”Cricket Australia’s eligibility confirmation said Anaya’s determination to commence in March 2027 would not be affected by amendments to its policy. It also confirmed that she is currently eligible to participate in Premier Cricket competitions in any Australian state or territory.For Anaya, the ambition is ultimately straightforward: “I would love to reach a point where I’m simply another cricketer competing against some of the best players in the world.”
Article Summary: Cricket Australia confirms Anaya Bangar will be eligible to play elite women's cricket in the country from March 2027. The decision opens a pathway for her to pursue a place in the Women’s Big Bash League (WBBL) Anaya described the development as an emotional moment after fearing that her cricket career had ended following her transition.

Article Title: ‘Really hacked off’: Carse in handcuffs leaves Root ‘really disappointed’ as England face fresh scrutiny
Article Text:
Brydon Carse and Joe Root

Root admits frustration over repeated incidents

From post-match beers to cultural reset

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

England captain Joe Root has admitted he is “really hacked off” and “really disappointed” after another off-field incident involving an England player brought the team's drinking culture under scrutiny again.Root's comments came after fast bowler Brydon Carse was pictured outside a nightclub in the early hours of Sunday in handcuffs and surrounded by police officers. The incident has prompted an investigation by England's Cricket Regulator and reignited questions over the team's conduct away from the field.The latest episode is particularly awkward for Root, who had only recently spoken about the responsibilities that come with representing England after the team leadership scrapped a midnight curfew imposed following a string of controversial late-night incidents.“Ultimately you’re grown adults,” Root had said after the curfew was removed. “You know what it takes to play for England, you know what your responsibilities are off the field, and we need to make sure we don’t find ourselves with any little situations off the field.”The latest incident appears to have tested Root's patience.“If I’m being brutally honest, I’m really hacked off. I’m really disappointed,” Root said at a news conference on Tuesday.“It’s not the isolated incident itself,” Root added. “It’s the fact we continually keep making stupid mistakes away from the game and it’s detracting from what we’re doing on the field.”Carse has yet to publicly comment on the incident, but Root said the fast bowler was deeply remorseful.“He’s very upset, has been very apologetic, and understands his actions.”Root was also blunt about the wider picture surrounding England's recent off-field episodes.“I don’t think it has been a very good look, the recent past, if I’m being brutally honest,” Root said. “At all.”The scrutiny comes despite the long-standing tradition of players sharing drinks after matches. Former England captain Ben Stokes himself spoke about the importance of celebrating with teammates after England's win over New Zealand at Lord's in June.“I probably won’t be real happy and smiley,” Stokes said at the time, “until I get up there and share a proper beer with the boys.”But a series of incidents has raised questions about where celebration ends and irresponsible behaviour begins.Former England captain Alastair Cook offered a blunt assessment on the Stick to Cricket podcast.“Just have some kind of brain cells amongst you, seeing what’s just gone on,” Cook said. “Surely someone says either don’t go to that place, or at 12 a.m. or 1 a.m. say, 'Let’s go and find ourselves somewhere quieter if we want to carry on.”
Article Summary: England captain Joe Root says he is'really hacked off' after off-field incident. Fast bowler Brydon Carse pictured outside a nightclub in the early hours of Sunday in handcuffs and surrounded by police officers. The incident has prompted an investigation by England's Cricket Regulator and reignited questions over the team's conduct away from the field.

Article Title: India vs Sri Lanka: The good, old grind takes centrestage in Colombo
Article Text:
Sri Lanka's Sonal Dinusha, assisted by a support staff member, on the third day of the second test match between India and Sri Lanka at the Sinhalese Sports Club Ground, in Colombo on Tuesday. (ANI)

TimesofIndia.com in Colombo:

India's Prasidh Krishna and teammates celebrate the wicket of Sri Lanka's Kamil Mishara on the third day of the second test match between India and Sri Lanka at the Sinhalese Sports Club Ground, in Colombo on Tuesday. (ANI Photo)

Key message is whenever we're playing Test cricket, it is a grind. As the boys walked in there, I said to them that it was a proper day of Test cricket, and this is how we're going to learn. Morne Morkel | Team India's bowling coach

A ground staff member walks on rain covers deployed on the ground as rain stops play on day 3 of the 2nd Test match between India and Sri Lanka, at the Sinhalese Sports Club ground in Colombo on Tuesday. (ANI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The setting during the final hour resembled that of the second day. The sky suddenly darkened, and the ground staff took position as grey clouds began to gather over the stadium. As the end of the third day drew near and the teams walked off the field, never to return, the feeling was familiar, yet somehow different.On both days, Sri Lanka were in survival mode, but on Tuesday, they kept India on the field for the entire day. The visitors dragged themselves along with slumped shoulders as they toiled for over 80 overs and will have to pick themselves up again for what looks like more hard work to enforce the follow-on. And then put on a brave face for the win."That'll be first prize if we can get those two wickets tomorrow early," said Morkel when asked about the team's thinking regarding enforcing the follow-on."With the weather around and sometimes the time it takes with taking the covers on and off, you know, we want to try and get as many overs as possible," added India's bowling coach.India had the ideal start on a very hot morning when Prasidh Krishna removed Kamil Mishra.Between the overs, the lanky fast bowler would often go down, holding his knees and catching that extra breath, but Shubman Gill never left his ear. The captain's usage of Krishna was enough to understand his reading of the pitch and why he felt that the Karnataka bowler was going to be the key on this surface with the extra bounce. This was the same bounce the opposition pair of Lahiru Kumara and Asitha Fernando used to their advantage on the first two days.Even in short bursts, the fast bowlers found the conditions and the flat track hard work, but Krishna ran in hard to create opportunities for his captain. It wasn't a surprise that Krishna took the second wicket in the morning session. He was rewarded for his persistent and consistent planning. After seeing the passage of play where every wicket came at a premium, the day also saw a period where two wickets fell in as many minutes off deliveries that shouldn't have taken wickets.Pasindu Sooriyabandara played one Ravindra Jadeja ball back onto his own stumps, and Niroshan Dickwella edged an innocuous Mohammed Siraj delivery down the leg side to Dhruv Jurel. Within the space of three deliveries, Sri Lanka were seven down with the scoreboard reading 173, and panic would have triggered in the home dressing room. They had been sitting with their feet up at 122/3 close to Lunch.There were plenty of oohs and aahs between those two events, but India were made to work hard. The odd ball gripped, a fair few turned, but Sri Lanka adeptly countered the challenge posed by the trio of Manav Suthar, Ravindra Jadeja and Saransh Jain. India let the game drift away with open fields in the second session and then towards the end when Sonal Dinusha frustrated the visitors with the tail.The tail came back to sting India, again, but it hurt the most on Tuesday as it didn't allow India another crack at Sri Lanka in fading light. For most of that period, the attention focused on getting rid of Lahiru, while Sonal continued his ways in a rather comfortable and open field setting. Result: They have already survived over 15 overs and look in no mood to throw their wickets away.For Morkel, it was a tough day of Test cricket, and he feels this experience will build character within the team for bigger challenges."Key message is whenever we're playing Test cricket, it is a grind. As the boys walked in there, I said to them that it was a proper day of Test cricket, and this is how we're going to learn. We always talk about bowling and partnerships. We always talk about creating pressure, you know, and this is how you learn it... when there's a partnership going, you can break it."The key is to find that breakthrough, and then how well can you start your next 10, 15 balls to the next better. And that is the young guys coming in, that is what they are going to experience and I welcome conditions and tough times like this because that's what builds character and that's how you're doing it great. So keep on rolling your best ball. That's all the role in partnerships. And find ways to be creative to maybe get us that sneaky one. We've got lucky that we have 500 on the board," said Morkel on the day India had.The equation and match situation is simple for India: Bowl out Sri Lanka as early as possible, enforce the follow-on and be ready to go hard at them again. There will be situations like the evening hour on both days, and it is up to the bowlers now to ensure they earn enough time to find those 12 wickets and seal a 2-0 series win.
Article Summary: Rain stops play on day 3 of the 2nd Test match between India and Sri Lanka in Colombo. Sri Lanka have already survived over 15 overs and look in no mood to throw their wickets away. India's bowling coach Morne Morkel: "Key message is whenever we're playing Test cricket, it is a grind"

Article Title: First in 48 years! Sonal Dinusha joins Zaheer Abbas, Everton Weekes in rare Test feat against India
Article Text:
Sri Lanka's Sonal Dinusha plays a shot on the third day of the second Test. (ANI Photo)

Dinusha's remarkable start against India

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Dinusha frustrates India as lower order digs in

NEW DELHI: Sri Lanka's Sonal Dinusha has entered an elite group of batters after becoming only the third player to score 80 or more in each of his first three Test innings against India, joining West Indies great Everton Weekes and Pakistan legend Zaheer Abbas Dinusha reached the landmark during a stubborn innings on the third day of the second Test in Colombo, remaining unbeaten on 85 as Sri Lanka finished at 265 for eight after rain and bad light forced an early close.The 25-year-old left-hander had already made 100 and 84 in his first two Test innings against India, and his latest effort made him the first batter since Abbas in 1978 to achieve the feat.Abbas had scored 176, 96 and 235 not out in his first three innings against India, while Weekes made 128, 194 and 162 in 1948. Weekes went on to score centuries in each of his first four innings against India before being dismissed for 90 in his fifth.Dinusha's latest innings also gave him a third consecutive 50-plus score against India, making him only the second Sri Lankan batter and 10th overall to achieve that feat in his first three Test innings against the opposition.The only Sri Lankan to previously accomplish it was Duleep Mendis, who scored 105, 105 and 51 in his first three Test innings against India.Dinusha's performance has been particularly striking given his comfort against spin. He has scored 106 runs through sweep shots — including conventional, slog and reverse sweeps — in the ongoing series, the most by a batter against spin in a Test series since ball-by-ball data became available in 2007 for the relevant shots.Joe Root holds the overall record in the category, having scored 160 runs through sweeps against Sri Lanka in 2021. Ben Duckett has 112 against Pakistan in 2022, while Root scored 106 against India in 2021.Dinusha has taken the sweep to another level in his short Test career. Of his 284 runs against spin, 122 — or 42.95 per cent — have come through sweep shots. He has scored those runs at a remarkable strike rate of 169.44, hitting 11 fours and four sixes without being dismissed playing the shot.India appeared to be closing in on Sri Lanka's innings when the hosts resumed after tea at 216 for seven. Instead, Dinusha continued to frustrate the attack for 201 minutes.He first added 57 runs with Keshara Nuwantha for the eighth wicket before putting on an unbeaten 35 with Lahiru Kumara for the ninth. Nuwantha faced 74 deliveries, while Kumara survived for 65 minutes off 50 balls.Earlier, India had claimed four wickets for 86 runs in the middle session after Sri Lanka had added 122 in the morning. Manav Suthar dismissed Dhananjaya de Silva, Ravindra Jadeja removed Pasindu Sooriyabandara for 80 and Mohammed Siraj accounted for Niroshan Dickwella.But Dinusha's resistance ensured Sri Lanka remained alive at 265 for eight, still 238 runs behind India's 503 for nine and 38 runs short of avoiding the follow-on.
Article Summary: Sonal Dinusha becomes only the third player to score 80 or more in each of his first three Test innings against India. Dinusha reached the landmark during a stubborn innings on the third day of the second Test in Colombo, remaining unbeaten on 85. Sri Lanka finished at 265 for eight after rain and bad light forced an early close.

Article Title: ‘Badly bruised’: Morne Morkel reveals why Rishabh Pant did not keep as Dhruv Jurel took gloves
Article Text:
Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel (ANI/PTI Photos)

Morkel backs Prasidh, praises Siraj

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India eye quick finish to enforce follow-on

NEW DELHI: India bowling coach Morne Morkel has revealed that Rishabh Pant's shoulder is “badly bruised” after the wicketkeeper-batter missed wicketkeeping duties on Day 3 in the second Test against Sri Lanka in Colombo.Pant suffered the injury on the opening day after taking a blow to his wrist and was forced to retire hurt. He returned on Day 2 and scored a brisk 63 off 89 balls, but did not take the field after India declared their first innings at 503 for nine.Dhruv Jurel, who scored a century on the second day, continued behind the stumps on Tuesday as Pant was kept away from the rigours of wicketkeeping as a precaution.“Rishabh Pant’s shoulder is badly bruised. He will be assessed overnight, we want his experience behind the stumps because he reads the game really well,” Morkel said at the post-day press conference.Pant's injury update came after India's bowlers were unable to finish off Sri Lanka on Day 3. The hosts reached 265 for eight before rain and bad light forced early stumps, with Sonal Dinusha unbeaten on 85.Morkel was particularly pleased with the character shown by Prasidh Krishna, who produced two lively spells and helped India regain momentum during the day.“Shows character of Prasidh Krishna… guy who had media and commentators on his back.As a team and management we knew about the potential, for him it was about silencing those voices. He lets go of thoughts, loves bowling, does homework and research. Massive student of the game. Has potential and talent to play all formats for a very long time.”He also praised Mohammed Siraj for his relentless effort on a difficult surface.“Siraj is a guy you want in your team. He can bowl all day from one end with a sore body. Even today, in flat conditions. He kept running in and has been the key guy for us. Quite lucky to have him in the team. Prasidh has extra pace and bounce. We need to use him in phases… it can be risky. The whole team is behind him and supporting him even when results don't go his way. It's my job to talk through these things and give him confidence…”Sri Lanka resumed from 8 for two but recovered through Pasindu Sooriyabandara's 80 and a series of lower-order partnerships. Dinusha then held firm for 201 minutes, adding 57 with Keshara Nuwantha and an unbeaten 35 with Lahiru Kumara.Sri Lanka still need 38 runs to avoid the follow-on after India posted 503 for nine.Morkel acknowledged the challenge posed by the home side's tail and stressed the importance of maintaining pressure after breakthroughs.“Test cricket is a grind. Tough conditions, hard conditions. The ball goes soft, it was a proper day of Test cricket. We always talk about bowling in partnerships and in pressure. Fun is to breakthrough and then how well you can start again. Follow-on will be India’s first target, we want to get those wickets quickly and be brave and put them in again,” Morne Morkel said.
Article Summary: India bowling coach Morne Morkel reveals Rishabh Pant's shoulder is 'badly bruised' The wicketkeeper-batter missed wicketkeeping duties on Day 3 in the second Test against Sri Lanka in Colombo. India declared their first innings at 503 for nine.

Article Title: 2nd Test: India struggle to finish off tail as Sonal Dinusha, Pasindu Sooriyabandara lead Sri Lanka resistance
Article Text:
Sri Lanka's Sonal Dinusha on day three of the second Test cricket match between India and Sri Lanka, in Colombo, Sri Lanka. (PTI Photo/Shailendra Bhojak)

Sri Lanka's lower order stands firm

Sooriyabandara, Mendis give Sri Lanka hope

India missed several chances to finish off Sri Lanka on Day 3 of the second Test as the hosts’ lower order put up a strong fight in Colombo.Led by Sonal Dinusha and Pasindu Sooriyabandara, Sri Lanka ended the day at 265/8, still 38 runs short of avoiding the follow-on.Dinusha remained unbeaten on 85 when rain and bad light brought play to an early close, while Lahiru Kumara was not out on 8. Dinusha continued his excellent run in the series, registering his third score above 50 in as many innings. He battled India’s pace and spin for 201 minutes and refused to give the bowlers an opening.He first added 57 runs with Keshara Nuwantha for the eighth wicket and then put on another 35 with Kumara. The long resistance from Sri Lanka’s tail frustrated India, who have struggled against lower-order batters in the past.Earlier, India appeared in control after reducing Sri Lanka to 216/7 by tea. Manav Suthar dismissed captain Dhananjaya de Silva, who edged to KL Rahul, while Ravindra Jadeja removed Sooriyabandara for a well-made 80. Mohammed Siraj then dismissed Niroshan Dickwella, caught behind by Dhruv Jurel.Sri Lanka had begun the day at 8/2 and quickly lost Kamil Mishara for 19, but Sooriyabandara and Kamindu Mendis changed the momentum with an 87-run partnership. Sooriyabandara, playing only his second Test, scored his maiden Test fifty from 76 balls and showed impressive composure.Mendis also attacked the Indian spinners, hitting Suthar for a six, before Prasidh Krishna ended the partnership by getting him to pull a short delivery straight to Jadeja.Despite India regaining control in the middle session, Dinusha and the lower order ensured Sri Lanka finished strongly. With 38 runs still needed to avoid the follow-on, India will hope to wrap up the innings quickly on Day 4.
Article Summary: Sonal Dinusha unbeaten on 85 when rain and bad light brought play to an early close. Dinusha battled India’s pace and spin for 201 minutes and refused to give the bowlers an opening. India appeared in control after reducing Sri Lanka to 216/7 by tea.

Article Title: 'You're just wasting time bro': Sarfaraz Khan's sledging skills go viral during IND vs SL 2nd Test - Watch

Sarfaraz gets under Sri Lanka's skin

Dickwella falls into India's trap

Article Title: Late-night incidents shaming English cricket: Cook says ‘Just have some kind of brain cells’
Article Text:
Brydon Carse nightclub incident (Screengrabs)

Brook’s club incident set the alarm bells ringing

Duckett and Stokes added to growing concerns

Carse incident brings scrutiny back

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

England’s cricketing culture is under fresh scrutiny after another late-night incident involving one of its players, raising questions over whether the traditional post-match drink has gone too far in an era of increasingly professional sport.The latest episode involved fast bowler Brydon Carse, who was pictured outside a nightclub in the early hours of Sunday in handcuffs and surrounded by police officers. The incident came just days after newly appointed England captain Joe Root had called for greater responsibility from the players.The England Cricket Regulator is investigating the matter, putting the spotlight back on the off-field behaviour of the men's squad and prompting questions over whether the team needs another cultural reset.Former England captain Alastair Cook believes the players need to exercise better judgement rather than necessarily abandon socialising altogether.“Just have some kind of brain cells amongst you, seeing what's just gone on,” Cook said on the Stick to Cricket podcast released Tuesday. “Surely someone says either don't go to that place, or at 12 a.m. or 1 a.m. say, 'Let's go and find ourselves somewhere quieter if we want to carry on.”The concerns are not new. England's problems with late-night behaviour began making headlines during their white-ball tour of New Zealand in October last year.A day before the third and final ODI, captain Harry Brook was hit by a bouncer after being denied entry to a club in Wellington. Jacob Bethell and Josh Tongue were also present during the night out.Brook was fined around £30,000 and given a final warning, although the sanctions only became public months later.“I want to apologise for my actions,” Brook said. “I fully accept that my behavior was wrong and brought embarrassment to both myself and the England team.”During the Ashes series in Australia, Ben Duckett's night out in Noosa also attracted attention after footage showed the England opener appearing disorientated and telling people he could not remember how to return to his hotel.“I am sorry for that incident, it was not professional and shouldn't have happened,” Duckett later said. “There is no hiding away from it.”England managing director Rob Key subsequently said he would investigate the team's drinking habits.The controversy intensified after England's home Test series against New Zealand. Following victory in the first Test at Lord's, Ben Stokes and Gus Atkinson continued celebrations with a night out in London. A member of England's security staff was reportedly struck by a Saracens rugby player during the evening.Stokes and Atkinson were left out of the second Test while the incident was investigated. The investigation ultimately found no “regulatory breach”, but the episode added to the growing scrutiny surrounding England's off-field culture.Stokes later announced his retirement from international cricket during the third Test, saying the previous few months had “taken its toll”. Brendon McCullum was subsequently dismissed as Test coach, while Key said the England and Wales Cricket Board was considering an alcohol ban.Carse's latest incident technically occurred while he was on domestic duty with Durham rather than with England. He had been released from the England squad to play against Derbyshire after not being selected for the first Test against Pakistan.However, Carse was subsequently retained in the squad for the second Test before being dropped on Monday as the investigation into the incident continued.According to Britain's Press Association, Carse was briefly arrested after the incident. England bowler Matthew Potts was also with him on the night out, while footage circulating on social media showed Stokes watching as Carse was held in handcuffs.The repeated incidents have revived the debate over England's drinking culture, with the central question no longer simply whether players should celebrate after matches, but whether a highly professional sporting setup needs clearer boundaries around how and where those celebrations take place.
Article Summary: Brydon Carse was pictured outside a nightclub in the early hours of Sunday in handcuffs and surrounded by police officers. The England Cricket Regulator is investigating the matter. England's problems with late-night behaviour began making headlines during their white-ball tour of New Zealand in October last year.

Article Title: 'I will continue to play for my father': Saransh Jain gets emotional after India Test debut
Article Text:
Saransh Jain

A special cap from Jadeja

Saransh Jain made his Test debut for India against Sri Lanka in Colombo on Sunday, becoming the 320th player to represent the country in Test cricket.The 33-year-old all-rounder came into the team in place of Kuldeep Yadav, but the biggest moment of his day was sharing the achievement with his family, especially his late father, who inspired him to play cricket.“First of all, I would like to thank God and after that my family. My father is the closest person to me, so I would tell him first (about making Test debut). I started playing cricket because of him, and I will continue to play for him," Saransh told BCCI after receiving his Test cap.Saransh Jain’s India debut is the result of years of struggle, patience and his father Subodh’s unwavering support.Diagnosed with mouth cancer in 2014, Subodh encouraged Saransh to continue cricket despite his son wanting to quit.After limited Ranji opportunities, Saransh flourished under Chandrakant Pandit, becoming a consistent all-rounder. His strong domestic record finally earned him his long-awaited India call-up.The occasion became even more meaningful when Ravindra Jadeja presented Saransh with his India cap. Saransh said he was happy to receive it from an experienced all-rounder who could motivate him.“Jaddu bhai is a legend and if I am getting the cap from him, it will only benefit me.I am very happy. I wanted to get a cap from an all-rounder who will motivate me. I am an all-rounder myself, so I will try to fulfil my dream," he added.Jadeja also encouraged the debutant to stay relaxed and treat the Test like another First-Class game. He praised Saransh's years of hard work in domestic cricket and India A.“Test cap No. 320, Saransh, well done," Jadeja said. “The hard work that you have done for so many years in domestic cricket and have performed continuously, be it India A or the Ranji Trophy, I think this is a very important opportunity for you in life."He added, “As a cricketer, everyone has a dream to represent India and become a Test player. You should enjoy this moment. Don’t take pressure at all."READ ALSO: 'I fought cancer to see my son play for India': Saransh Jain's long road to Test cricket Jadeja further reminded Saransh that he had already handled tough domestic matches and had the full support of his teammates.“Just like you have performed in so many domestic matches, play like you are playing another First-Class match. You have all the other 14 players with you to support you. Enjoy this moment instead of taking pressure," he added.
Article Summary: Saransh Jain made his Test debut for India against Sri Lanka on Sunday. The 33-year-old all-rounder became the 320th player to represent the country in Test cricket. Saransh said the biggest moment of his day was sharing the achievement with his family, especially his late father.

NEW DELHI: Tripura chief minister Manik Saha has fulfilled a promise made to Commonwealth Games gold medallist Asmita Dey, with the state government allotting her a piece of land in Agartala to build a house.The 23-year-old judoka was honoured in Tripura on Wednesday after becoming the first Indian judoka to win a Commonwealth Games gold medal.Dey won the women’s -48kg title in Glasgow after defeating Canada’s Heidi Quach in a dramatic golden-score contest.
